findings.body:
**Keep preview writes inside the resolved output tree.**

If `--output/systemd` is a symlink to the user's live systemd unit directory, Line 911 accepts it because that directory is outside the checkout. Line 922 then replaces installed unit files through the symlink. Before any preview write, require each resolved child to stay inside the resolved preview root. Ordinary `systemd` and `launchd` subdirectories still pass.
findings.title: Keep preview writes inside the resolved output tree.

findings.body:
**Reject duplicate unit basenames before writing any unit.**

If the pinned tree contains both `crq-repair.service` and `extra/crq-repair.service`, both templates write to the same output file. `prepare` then verifies the final file twice and records only its digest. Check for duplicate basenames before creating the output files. Unique basenames should still render normally.
findings.title: Reject duplicate unit basenames before writing any unit.

findings.body:
**Do not treat a failed Git probe as proof that a path is outside Git.**

If Git detects a checkout owned by another account, it can refuse the probe with a dubious-ownership error. Line 205 accepts that result. A mode-0600 overlay in that checkout then passes `load_overlay` if the checkout is separate from `deploy_root`. `record` has the same gap. Distinguish a confirmed non-repository from a failed probe. Reject the failed probe without changing Git's trust settings. ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/git/git/v2.52.0/setup.c))
findings.title: Do not treat a failed Git probe as proof that a path is outside Git.

findings.body:
**Prevent unit activation throughout the checkout switch.**

If systemd accepts a start request after the final `inactive` check, it can dispatch the unit while `switch` restores the committed config, changes HEAD, or writes the destination config. `tick_lock` serializes helper operations but does not block systemd activation. Require an activation barrier that covers the full mutation window on the direct CLI path as well as the managed path. Another `list-jobs` call would only take another snapshot. ([freedesktop.org](https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemctl))
findings.title: Prevent unit activation throughout the checkout switch.

findings.body:
**Recognize `ExecStart` with valid whitespace around `=`.**

A committed template with one `ExecStart = ...` is valid systemd syntax. Line 632 counts zero directives and rejects it. The bulk Node renderer rejects the same template at Line 447. Use one directive parser for counting and replacement. Keep exact-one validation and continuation handling. ([freedesktop.org](https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/256/systemd.syntax.html?utm_source=openai))






Also applies to: 632-632
findings.title: Recognize `ExecStart` with valid whitespace around `=`.

findings.body:
**Bind rollback to the current deployment transaction.**

At Line 2170, matching `HEAD` proves only that the supplied record names the same deployed commit. If two hosts reached B from different commits, host 2 can accept host 1's genuine A→B journal and roll back to A instead of its own prior commit C. The tag and compatibility checks validate A as a target, not as host 2's prior target.

Require the supplied record to match the locally retained transaction for the current deployment before using its `prior_head`.
findings.title: Bind rollback to the current deployment transaction.

findings.body:
**Capture the preservation baseline after the drain.**

At Line 1511, `preflight` hashes the queue and heartbeat before the stopped-unit and drain checks. If a final tick publishes both files and exits before those checks, the checks pass and the helper switches the checkout. Line 1527 then reports a preservation failure against the old digests, although the helper changed neither file.

Capture the preservation digests after the stopped-unit check and successful drain. Keep the post-helper comparison so it still catches writes during the switch.
findings.title: Capture the preservation baseline after the drain.

findings.body:
**Record the result of a failed recovery attempt.**

If `restore_activation` partially succeeds and then raises, Lines 1662–1663 copy the old `outcome` into the exception. The CLI can exit 3 with `outcome: "pending"`, and the journal has no record of the new failure.

Save and emit `outcome: "recovery_required"` with the last retained phase and the new failure reason. If that write fails, report the write error and the retained record path. Keep `rolled_back` for successful recovery.
findings.title: Record the result of a failed recovery attempt.

findings.body:
**Wait for the first heartbeat on a fresh host.**

If the runner has not yet published `heartbeat.json`, Line 1353 raises before the first-tick polling callback runs. The health command exits 2 even if the runner publishes within `--first-tick-timeout-seconds`.

Use the first-tick budget to wait for an initially absent heartbeat. Continue to reject unreadable or foreign heartbeats, and require a second advancing tick.
findings.title: Wait for the first heartbeat on a fresh host.

findings.body:
**Report unsupported receipt types without losing the health result.**

If the deployment receipt schema uses `type: "number"` for a property present in a sampled local-review receipt, Line 1035 raises `KeyError`. The sample and CLI handlers do not catch it. The command loses both the receipt verdict and the tick result.

Return an unsupported-schema diagnostic for type names outside `_SCHEMA_TYPES`. Keep that diagnostic in the receipt verdict. As per coding guidelines, “Every operation invocation writes machine-readable JSON to stdout and human narration to stderr, never mixed.”
findings.title: Report unsupported receipt types without losing the health result.

findings.body:
**Return a JSON error when the helper cannot compile.**

If the readable helper has a syntax error and no digest pin is supplied, Line 82 raises `SyntaxError` before the controller lock. The CLI does not catch it. With `--json`, stdout stays empty and stderr receives a traceback.

Translate the compile failure at the helper-load boundary. Keep the existing hash check and execute only the bytes that were hashed. As per coding guidelines, “In machine mode (`--json`) stderr stays empty.”
findings.title: Return a JSON error when the helper cannot compile.

findings.body:
**Bind the unit switch to the commit observed under the controller lock.**

`production_adapter` reads `HEAD` before `switch_unit` takes the controller lock. The adapter renders the unit at that commit. `switch_unit` then records a `prior_head` read under the lock. If another controller moves `HEAD` in between, the unit installs from the old commit while the journal records the new one. Recovery later composes the prior runtime at the journaled commit, so the recorded commit no longer identifies the rendered source.

Under the controller lock, before `journal_append`, refuse the switch when the live `HEAD` differs from the commit the adapter was composed from. Alternatively, compose the adapter under the lock. In either case, the installed source and the recorded `prior_head` must come from the same observed `HEAD`.
findings.title: Bind the unit switch to the commit observed under the controller lock.

findings.body:
**Keep admission held if writing the expired-drain record fails.**

If the queue drain expires and writing `drain.json` raises `ENOSPC`, the write fails before the code raises `FailStop`. `recover()` then attempts pre-switch restoration. If the active run has not changed the queue or heartbeat bytes, restoration can restart triggers and remove the marker while that run is still live.

Make expiry enter fail-stop regardless of whether the evidence write succeeds. Preserve the write error in the recovery result. Keep the normal path for a drain that settles before the deadline.
findings.title: Keep admission held if writing the expired-drain record fails.

findings.body:
**Return the recovery record when it cannot be written.**

If `fail_stop()` cannot write `deploy.json`, it attaches the recovery record and `persistence_error` to `RecoveryRequired`. The CLI only emits `run_dir`, `outcome`, and a truncated message. The operator loses the original trigger map, runtime measurement, and structured storage error when the file that should contain them is unavailable.

Include the recovery record in the single JSON error artifact when persistence fails. Preserve exit code 3.
findings.title: Return the recovery record when it cannot be written.

findings.body:
**Enforce the queue drain deadline before accepting a late poll.**

With `--drain-deadline-s 10 --drain-interval-s 600`, a blocked initial poll can sleep for 600 seconds. If the queue settles after 30 seconds, the next poll returns `drained=True` and the deploy proceeds without checking the deadline.

Cap each sleep at the remaining time. Do not accept a success observed after expiry. Preserve immediate success when the first poll finds the queue drained.
findings.title: Enforce the queue drain deadline before accepting a late poll.

findings.body:
**Return JSON for help in machine mode.**

`--json deploy --help` invokes argparse's default help action. It prints plain text to stdout and exits before `main()` dispatches the operation. The `error()` override does not handle help. ([docs.python.org](https://docs.python.org/3/library/argparse.html))

Handle help on the shared parser so both root and subcommand help return one JSON artifact in machine mode. As per coding guidelines, “Every operation invocation writes machine-readable JSON to stdout and human narration to stderr, never mixed.”
findings.title: Return JSON for help in machine mode.

findings.body:
**Give operators a recovery step that can clear this refusal.**

The message tells the operator to install and verify the target unit definitions first. If the operator does that and retries against the same prior and target SHAs, the committed blobs still differ and the runbook refuses again. The guard does not inspect installed definitions.

State that this runbook cannot deploy a unit-template change. If a supported coordinated checkout and unit workflow exists, name it instead. Keep the refusal before any trigger stops.
findings.title: Give operators a recovery step that can clear this refusal.

findings.body:
**Reject a missing runtime entry before taking the admission hold.**

If the absolute `repair.cq_bin` path is already missing, `measure_cq_bin()` records `exists=False`. Preflight accepts it, and the post-drain equality check accepts the same missing entry. After the switch, `runtime_pointer_check()` rejects it. Rollback can restore the prior SHA and config but still fails the same runtime check before restarting triggers.

Require an existing entry for a non-placeholder pointer at preflight. Keep the later checks so deletion after preflight is still detected.
findings.title: Reject a missing runtime entry before taking the admission hold.
